about: Build queue. Work the 'ready' items top to bottom without re-asking the owner; they are decided. 'blocked' items wait on what 'blocked_on' says. When an item is done, delete it here and add a 'done' entry to progress.json (replacing its 'planned' entry if it has one).

items.blocked_on: The brothers' look (open question in needs.json; a stand-in can be used). Fortresses and warlords are built; the Seal of the Seven drops after all seven.
items.title: Campaign, part 4: the hidden warlord (secretly the good guy)
items.decided: Owner, 2026-10-07: campaign endgame. Random mixed raids start wars; beating a faction's raids opens its warlord's fortress in its homeland; you march on it; own race's renegades last; then the hidden warlord behind the wars. Rewards: base trophy, warlord gear, Warlord title. Owner, 2026-10-07: he is the advisor's brother; on defeat he dies and hands over his blade and the key to the End. Owner, 2026-10-07: his fortress is the frozen battlefield of the brothers' first war, a pocket dimension reached by joining the seven War Maps; the brothers share one face and build.
spec: Identity: the advisor's brother, same ancient power. He set the factions against the player to stop the advisor's chosen champion from rising.

On defeat he dies: a short dying scene (chat/toast-style lines) reveals the advisor is his brother and the true enemy, then drops his blade (unique weapon, any race) and the Key to the End, which triggers campaign-betrayal.

Fortress: a Warfront pocket dimension ('the Frozen Field'): a battlefield sealed out of time under a still, colorless sky, with stone statues of armies of all seven races caught mid-fight, broken siege engines and banners. Structures: outer field, a ruined war camp of mixed race styles, and his keep at the center. Fought there using every race's tricks across his phases; statues near him can wake up as defenders at phase changes.

Entry: after all seven warlords, combining the seven War Maps (crafting or right-click with all seven) makes the Sealed Map; using it at a War Standard opens a portal there. Your whole army can march through. Leaving or losing returns you home.

Look: same face and build as the advisor's true form, but scarred and armored. Until the owner designs them, use a stand-in: tall knight in worn, mismatched armor, a cracked crown, gray and faded gold.

items.blocked_on: The advisor's true form (open question in needs.json); also campaign-final-boss built first.
items.title: Campaign, part 5: the betrayal and the fight in the End
items.decided: Owner, 2026-10-07: one villain in seven disguises is each race's advisor, runs the tutorial, is revealed after the hidden warlord falls (who was trying to stop him), and is fought in the End with only your heroes and beasts against a mixed army.
spec: After the hidden warlord's dying reveal, the advisor appears, drops his disguise (short scene) and teleports the player to the End main island with only their Captains, Champions and war beasts (fallen or returning heroes come back for this fight). Rank-and-file troops stay home.
Compatibility: require the vanilla Ender Dragon to be beaten first (the End is then empty); the advisor's dragon is a Warfront 'bound dragon' entity, so the vanilla fight state isn't touched.
He holds the island with waves of mixed troops from all seven races and his own towers, in phases: army, towers and summons, then he mounts the bound dragon for the last phase.
Losing returns the player home (heroes fall as usual); the fight can be retried.
Victory: the End is freed, credits-style closing lines, a final trophy and the campaign marked complete.

items.blocked_on: Node lists for the seven race paths (open question in needs.json). The six shared paths are designed; they can be built first.
items.title: Player skill tree: Renown, six shared paths, race paths, active skill slots
items.decided: Owner, 2026-10-07: build freedom over race-locked kits. Shared playstyle paths plus one race path, Renown points from battle, small race affinity, Warfront's own system, cooldowns only.
spec: Renown: a player attachment (XP and level), synced. Gains: kills (small, more for Captains/Champions/beasts), raid or siege wave won, raider camp cleared, warlord beaten (large, plus 1 bonus skill point each). Level curve tuned so a player reaches about level 10 by base level 3 and about 25 by the end of the campaign. 1 skill point per level. Total points by the end: enough for about two and a half paths plus some of the race path.

Paths (shared by all races): Blade (melee; works with any weapon in #minecraft:swords, #minecraft:axes and spear/other melee tags, so Better Combat, Simply Swords and Epic Knights weapons all count), Bulwark (shield and armor), Marksman (bows, crossbows, tridents and thrown weapons), Arcane (boosts Iron's Spells through its attributes; without Iron's Spells, its nodes boost Warfront's own magic damage), Skirmisher (mobility and stealth), Commander (army buffs, army cap, beasts). Plus one race path per race that deepens the race power.

Nodes: about 10 per path in a short branching tree; each needs its parent. Most are passives (vanilla attribute modifiers or event hooks); 2-3 per path are active skills. Data-driven (JSON nodes in the mod's data folder) so nodes can be tuned without code.
Active skills: up to 4 equipped in skill slots (keybinds, rebindable), from any path. Cooldowns only, no new mana bar.

Race affinity: each race has 2 favored paths where the first 3 nodes cost nothing. Proposed: Human Blade + Commander, Elf Marksman + Skirmisher, Dwarf Bulwark + Blade, Orc Blade + Bulwark, Demon Arcane + Skirmisher, Angel Arcane + Bulwark, Hive Skirmisher + Commander (owner can change).
Respec: at the War Table, refund all points for Mana Crystals (cost grows with points spent).
UI: a Skill Tree screen in the ui-foundation theme (race accent color), opened from the War Table and a hotkey; skill slots on the combat HUD next to the race power; a Renown bar.
Test Panel and /wftest: grant Renown or levels, grant points, unlock any node, reset the tree.

Game tests: Renown rises from a kill and a level grants a point; a node can't be bought without its parent; a passive node applies its attribute and respec removes it; affinity nodes cost 0 for the right race.

Blade path nodes (owner-approved 2026-10-07): Keen Edge (+6% melee damage) -> Swift Hands (+10% attack speed) -> Duelist branch: Precise Strike (ACTIVE: next hit ignores armor and crits, 10 s), Executioner (+25% damage to enemies under 30% health), Bleeding Cuts (crits apply a bleed DoT); Reaver branch: Cleave (ACTIVE: wide arc hitting everything in front, 10 s), Wide Arcs (sweep hits +50%), Bloodlust (kills give +10% attack speed for 5 s, stacks 3) -> Battle Hardened (heal 2 on kill; needs either branch's last node) -> Blade Storm (ACTIVE capstone: 3 s whirl striking everything around you, 40 s). Counts any weapon in melee weapon tags.

Bulwark path nodes (owner-approved 2026-10-07): Iron Skin (+2 armor) -> Shield Training (shield raises faster, axe-disable time halved) -> Sentinel branch: Shield Wall (ACTIVE: block from every direction for 4 s, 20 s), Unshakable (+30% knockback resistance), Steel Thorns (shield blocks reflect 20% of melee damage); Vanguard branch: Shield Bash (ACTIVE: stun the first enemy in front 1.5 s, 10 s), Provoke (enemies you hit target you for 5 s), Momentum (sprinting into enemies with shield raised knocks them aside) -> Last Stand (once per 2 min a killing blow leaves you at 1 health with Resistance III for 3 s) -> Guardian's Aegis (ACTIVE capstone: for 8 s, half the damage allies within 6 blocks take is redirected to you, 60 s).

Marksman path nodes (owner-approved 2026-10-07): Steady Aim (+8% projectile damage, tighter spread) -> Quick Draw (bow draw and crossbow reload 20% faster) -> Sniper branch: Piercing Shot (ACTIVE: next shot pierces every enemy in line with +50% damage, 12 s), Hawkeye (+20% damage on hits from 20+ blocks), Headhunter (+15% damage vs Captains, Champions and bosses); Ranger branch: Volley (ACTIVE: next shot fires 5 projectiles in a cone, 14 s), Run and Gun (no movement slowdown while drawing or aiming), Retrieval (40% chance not to use ammo) -> Hunter's Mark (your hits make the target glow for 5 s and your army deals it +10% damage) -> Rain of Arrows (ACTIVE capstone: arrows rain on a 6-block area for 4 s, 45 s). Works for any item in bow, crossbow, trident and thrown-weapon tags.

Arcane path nodes (owner-approved 2026-10-07): Attunement (+5% spell power via Iron's spell_power attribute) -> Focus (-10% spell cooldowns via Iron's cooldown_reduction) -> Battlemage branch: Spellblade (ACTIVE: for 6 s, melee hits add magic damage of your race's strong Iron's school, 15 s), Arcane Armor (10% of damage taken is paid from Iron's mana instead), Mana Strike (melee hits restore a little Iron's mana); Evoker branch: Overcharge (ACTIVE: next spell +40% spell power, 20 s), Deep Well (+20% max mana, +15% mana regen), Spell Echo (10% chance a cast spell's cooldown resets) -> Ley Tap (Iron's mana regenerates 2x while inside your base's mana network, pylon range) -> Arcane Surge (ACTIVE capstone: 8 s of no mana cost and halved cooldowns, 75 s). Without Iron's Spells: spell-power nodes boost Warfront magic damage (race powers, Spellblade), mana nodes turn into skill cooldown reduction.

Skirmisher path nodes (owner-approved 2026-10-07): Fleet Foot (+8% move speed) -> Light Landing (no fall damage under 6 blocks, half above) -> Shadow branch: Vanish (ACTIVE: invisible 4 s and nearby enemies drop you as a target, 25 s), Ambush (first hit from invisibility or from behind +50% damage), Quiet Step (sneaking makes no sound or vibration, so sculk sensors and Wardens miss you); Outrider branch: Dash (ACTIVE: 6-block dash in the move direction, 2 charges, 8 s per charge), Hit and Run (after landing a hit, +20% speed for 2 s), Slippery (15% chance to dodge a melee hit) -> Opportunist (+20% damage to slowed, rooted, stunned or routing enemies) -> Shadow Dance (ACTIVE capstone: for 6 s Dash has no cooldown and hitting a new enemy makes you invisible for 1 s, 60 s).

Commander path nodes (owner-approved 2026-10-07): Formations are NOT gated: every player keeps all formations. Drillmaster (your units +5% max health) -> Logistics (+2 army cap) -> Empowerer branch: Kindle Arms (ACTIVE: for 10 s your units within 16 blocks add your race's strong-school element to their hits: Human Evocation arcane burst, Elf Nature poison, Dwarf Lightning chain spark, Orc Blood lifesteal for the unit, Demon Fire ignite, Angel Holy bonus vs undead/demons/Hive, Hive Eldritch armor shred; 30 s), Blood Bond (5% of the damage your units deal heals you), Shared Armor (units within 10 blocks gain 15% of your armor value as an attribute modifier); Warmaster branch: Call to Arms (ACTIVE: up to 6 of your units at your base teleport to your side, 90 s), Beastmaster (+1 war beast slot, never above 10), Veteran Corps (units gain veterancy XP 25% faster) -> Steady Ranks (your units within 12 blocks rout half as often) -> Last Order (ACTIVE capstone: every fallen hero of yours within 24 blocks gets up at half health, 120 s).

items.title: Race towers, wave 1: the system plus the seven level 2 towers
items.decided: Owner, 2026-10-07: 3 race towers per race (base level 2, 3, 5), own race only, race towers capped by base level, capstones 1 each.
spec: System: a RaceTower base (block + block entity) with race, unlock level and cap group. Placement checks: placer's race matches, the base on that mana network is at the unlock level, and the race-tower cap isn't reached (2/4/6/10 for base levels 2-5; capstones max 1 each). Refuse with a toast (ui-foundation) or action-bar message saying why.
Count placed race towers per base (stored with the base data); breaking one frees the slot. Losing base level doesn't remove towers, but blocks new ones over the cap.
Human: Ballista: long-range bolt that pierces a line of enemies; bonus damage to beasts and large mobs.
Elf: Thornwood Sentinel: roots the nearest enemies in vines (heavy slow, short root) and marks them Glowing so archers focus them.
Dwarf: Rune Cannon: slow heavy shot, splash damage on impact, no block damage.
Orc: War Drum Totem: support: orc units within 12 blocks gain Rage faster; each drum beat has a chance to make nearby enemies flee briefly.
Demon: Soul Pyre: sets enemies on fire; kills near it charge it, and at 10 charges it unleashes a fire burst.
Angel: Sun Lance: holy beam; strong by day with open sky, weak at night; bonus damage to demons, Hive and undead.
Hive: Lurker Pit: hidden in the ground until enemies come close, then ambushes with acid that lowers armor; stronger underground.

Every race tower is a block entity on the base mana network like the existing towers (draws mana per shot or pulse; no mana, no effect) and reuses the tower friend-or-foe targeting. Placeholder models are generated and styled in the race palette, following the tower-models item; final looks can follow references later. Numbers live in config. Codex: a render and a one-line description per tower.
Game tests: wrong race can't place; under-level base can't place; cap enforced; each tower acts only with mana; one effect test per tower (assert on a counter or state).

items.title: Race towers, wave 2: the seven level 3 towers
items.decided: Owner, 2026-10-07: 3 race towers per race (base level 2, 3, 5), own race only, race towers capped by base level, capstones 1 each.
spec: Human: Watchtower Bell: no attack; reveals invisible and tunneling enemies within 24 blocks (Glowing), +25% range to towers within 8 blocks, rings when a raid enters range.
Elf: Moonwell Grove: slow heal pulse for elf units and the owner within 10 blocks; cheap on mana.
Dwarf: Stone Warden: tough turret block with high health that taunts enemies within 10 blocks to attack it.
Orc: Goblin Bomb Catapult: lobs bombs in an arc, area damage, no block damage.
Demon: Brimstone Chains: grabs the nearest enemy, pulls it in and holds it for a few seconds.
Angel: Choir Bell: shields nearby friendly units (absorption) and clears harmful effects on a pulse.
Hive: Brood Nest: spawns short-lived swarmlings that rush enemies.

Every race tower is a block entity on the base mana network like the existing towers (draws mana per shot or pulse; no mana, no effect) and reuses the tower friend-or-foe targeting. Placeholder models are generated and styled in the race palette, following the tower-models item; final looks can follow references later. Numbers live in config. Codex: a render and a one-line description per tower.
Game tests: one effect test per tower; the level 3 unlock is enforced.

items.title: Race towers, wave 3: the seven level 5 capstones
items.decided: Owner, 2026-10-07: 3 race towers per race (base level 2, 3, 5), own race only, race towers capped by base level, capstones 1 each.
spec: Human: Trebuchet: very long range (48+) slow boulder with splash damage that doesn't break blocks; can target and damage enemy siege outposts.
Elf: Elder Treant Spire: at each wave start wakes a treant guardian (temporary tanky unit) that fights until the wave ends.
Dwarf: Thunder Forge: chain lightning that jumps between up to 5 enemies; uses Iron's Lightning spell power when present.
Orc: Waaagh Banner: every orc unit within 16 blocks starts each siege wave in Frenzy.
Demon: Hellgate: spawns temporary imps (Impalers/Firecasters) each wave, paid with mana; they vanish at wave end.
Angel: Seraphic Obelisk: calls a pillar of light on the strongest enemy in range for a heavy smite.
Hive: Synapse Spire: pulses confusion: enemies in range briefly attack each other.
Capstones are limited to one per base each, and count toward the race-tower cap.
Temporary summons (treant, imps, swarmlings from Brood Nest) despawn at wave end, don't count toward the army cap or beastLimit, and never drop loot.

Placeholder models are generated and styled in the race palette, following the tower-models item; final looks can follow references later. Numbers live in config. Codex: a render and a one-line description per tower.
Game tests: the one-per-base limit; summons despawn; the Trebuchet can damage an outpost.

items.title: Crossover: homelands and mana fuel
items.decided: Owner, 2026-10-07: replace Twilight Forest with The Aether and Deeper and Darker, and cross them over with Warfront (all four crossovers).
spec: Optional integration like Iron's Spells: check ModList.isLoaded and use tags/registry lookups by id, no hard dependency; Warfront must still load and pass tests without either mod.

Homelands: angels get the race's 'home' bonus in the Aether dimension (aether:the_aether) and the Hive gets its underground bonus everywhere in the Otherside (deeperdarker:otherside), sunlight weakness never applies there. Add a dimension check next to the existing Hive underground logic.
Raids: Fallen Host warbands spawn freely in the Aether, Swarm warbands in the Otherside (NpcFaction homeland predicates take the dimension too). Overworld sieges are unchanged.

Mana: new item tags warfront:mana_fuel/shard_grade and crystal_grade, filled optionally with Aether Ambrosium Shard (shard grade) and Zanite Gemstone (crystal grade), and Deeper and Darker sculk bone / echo-type materials (pick real item ids from the mod's registry at build time). Mana Wells accept anything in the tags. Use tag entries with required:false so missing mods are fine.
Game tests can't load the other mods: test the tag path with a vanilla item added to the tag in a test datapack, and the dimension check via a helper.

items.title: Crossover: Aether wings recipe and Moa, Otherside echo armor
items.decided: Owner, 2026-10-07: replace Twilight Forest with The Aether and Deeper and Darker, and cross them over with Warfront (all four crossovers).
spec: Optional integration like Iron's Spells: check ModList.isLoaded and use tags/registry lookups by id, no hard dependency; Warfront must still load and pass tests without either mod.
Angel wings (mechanics from the angel-wings item): add an Aether recipe from boss loot (Valkyrie or Sun Spirit drops) plus Mana Crystals when the Aether is loaded; the vanilla fallback recipe stays.

Angel war beast: an armored Moa, summoned at the altar like the Deepmaw (counts against beastLimit); own model in Warfront, not the Aether's entity, so it works without the Aether. Its altar unlock needs an Aether item when the Aether is loaded.

Hive echo armor (owner, 2026-10-07): a 4-piece set, Hive players only, crafted from Deeper and Darker echo materials plus Mana Crystals; without that mod, a fallback recipe from echo shards and sculk.

Bonuses through vanilla attributes/effects: armor about diamond level; each piece adds damage and toughness when the wearer is in darkness or underground (no sky, low light); the full set gives quieter steps (sculk sensors and wardens ignore walking, the vibration-dampening tag behaviour) and short night vision in caves.
Placeholder look: dark teal chitin plates with cyan vein glow, generated like the other textures; the final look follows the Hive player reference.
Game tests: the set's dark bonus applies underground and not under open sky; non-Hive players can't equip it.

items.title: Crossover: outposts in the Aether and the Otherside
items.decided: Owner, 2026-10-07: replace Twilight Forest with The Aether and Deeper and Darker, and cross them over with Warfront (all four crossovers).
spec: Optional integration like Iron's Spells: check ModList.isLoaded and use tags/registry lookups by id, no hard dependency; Warfront must still load and pass tests without either mod.
Reuse the siege outpost structures and raid chests as world structures: Fallen Host fort-sized outposts on Aether islands, Swarm outposts in Otherside caverns.
Guarded by their faction, no siege attached; loot the chest and break it to clear the outpost, same as sieges. Loot one tier above the wave-15 siege table: late-game raid targets.
Rare: about one per few hundred blocks (structure set spacing), configurable.
